meaning: The number of descendants of Pahath-Moab (from the families of Joshua and Joab) in the census after the exile, as recorded in Nehemiah 7:11.
description: The number 2818 appears in Nehemiah 7:11 in connection with the listing of those who returned from the Babylonian exile to Judah. It indicates the number of descendants of Pahath-Moab, specifically from the lineage of Joshua and Joab. Pahath-Moab (Hebrew: פַּחַת מוֹאָב, "governor of Moab") was a prominent family among those who returned, and their large numbers testify to the significance this clan held in the restored community. The censuses in Ezra and Nehemiah serve an important theological function: they emphasize God's faithfulness in preserving a remnant of His people through the exile and bringing them back to the promised land, in accordance with prophetic promises.

versions.meaning: The number 2818 has no known established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: The number 2818 does not appear as a specific symbolic number in the Bible or in well-known Jewish numerological traditions (gematria). Biblical number symbolism typically focuses on numbers such as 3, 7, 12, 40, and similar. Although one might attempt to break down 2818 into smaller components and interpret them, there is no recognized tradition that assigns this number any special spiritual or symbolic meaning.
versions.reason: [critical] The number 2818 appears explicitly in Nehemiah 7:11 as the count of descendants of Pahath-Moab (from the lineage of Joshua and Joab). This is entirely omitted from both meaning and description, which incorrectly claim that the number has no known occurrence or significance.; [critical] The meaning field states that the number 'has no known established symbolic meaning', but the number is a concrete biblical figure used in the post-exilic census in Nehemiah 7:11.; [major] The description claims that the number 'does not appear as a specific number in the Bible', which is factually incorrect—it appears in Nehemiah 7:11 as an exact census figure.; [minor] It is worth noting the parallel passage in Ezra 2:6, where the same family is counted as 2812, and the difference between these numbers is an interesting textual-critical point suitable for a footnote.

footnotes.text: In the parallel passage in Ezra 2:6, the number of descendants of Pahath-Moab is given as 2812, six fewer than in Nehemiah 7:11. Such numerical differences between the two lists are common and may be due to different times of registration, copyist errors in transmission, or differing criteria for who was counted.

The name פַּחַת מוֹאָב (Pahat-Moab) literally means "the governor of Moab" and may point back to a time when an Israelite leader had authority over the region of Moab, possibly during the reigns of David or Solomon (cf. 2 Sam 8:2).

The descendants of Pahath-Moab are also mentioned among those who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Neh 10:14), showing that this family continued to play a leading role in the restored community in Jerusalem.
